主要内容: On June 4, 2019, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) unveiled amendments to the Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR), respectively. These changes, announced on April 17, 2019, aim to implement the President’s foreign policy on Cuba by restricting non-family travel to Cuba and ending exports of passenger vessels, recreational vessels, and private aircraft. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin emphasized that these actions are part of a strategic decision to reverse the loosening of sanctions and keep U.S. dollars out of the hands of Cuban military, intelligence, and security services. The Treasury changes will take effect on June 5, 2019, when the regulations are published in the Federal Register. OFAC’s amendments include a 'grandfathering' provision for group people-to-people educational travel that had already been authorized before June 5, 2019. BIS is also amending the EAR to deny license exceptions for certain vessels and aircraft. These regulatory changes align with the National Security Presidential Memorandum signed on June 16, 2017, titled 'Strengthening the Policy of the United States Toward Cuba.'

股票实体.名称: U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
